header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: James Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Connor Liu (Redwood Solutions), Maya Ortiz (Avalon - Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Avalon - Backend), Ravi Patel (Avalon - CTO), Sofia Gomez (Avalon - Data Eng)
summary: Discovery call to understand Avalon's current vector search stack, throughput and latency goals, and evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for embeddings + reranking. Key concerns: hybrid search with BM25 + embeddings, vector DB integration (they use Pinecone/Elastic), dimensionality and cost tradeoffs, latency SLOs, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed next steps: provide pricing, security docs, run a throughput sizing deep dive, and customer to share sample data.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
security/compliance: SOC2, VPC, KMS, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] James: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm James from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we have Priya the systems engineer and Connor who's helping with solution fit. can you all do quick intros?
[00:14] Maya: sure, maya here, head of ML at Avalon. we own the search + recommendations team.
[00:20] Daniel: daniel, backend eng, i own the vec infra and current pinecone setup.
[00:26] Ravi: ravi, cto, hopping on for high level constraints.
[00:31] James: great, thanks. quick agenda: understand your current stack, goals for embeddings + rerank, perf and cost constraints, and then discuss redwood deployment options.
[00:45] Maya: high level: we're running a hybrid retrieval flow — bm25 for recall then embeddings for rerank. currently store vectors in Pinecone, some fallback to Elastic for older indices.
[00:57] Priya: when you say hybrid, do you run late interaction or just re-rank top-k?
[01:03] Maya: we do top-100 from bm25 then embed rerank top 10. latency target is end-to-end 200-300ms for search, p95 under 500ms.
[01:18] Connor: okay, and what's your qps right now?
[01:21] Daniel: it's bursty, avg 30 qps but peaks to 250 qps during events. we're cloud hosted on GCP, so autoscaling matters.
[01:31] James: good to know. what embedding model and vector dimensionality are you using?
[01:36] Maya: custom finetuned 1024-d vectors using an open model from last year. cost is already a concern — storing 100M vectors is pricey and the rerank compute on each query adds up.
[01:50] Priya: are you doing async caching or prefix caching now? any kv cache?
[01:54] Daniel: we tried an LRU prefix cache but miss rates were high; we don't have a kv cache per se, more application-level caching.
[02:05] Ravi: also important: data residency, we need EU copies for some customers.
[02:10] James: thanks, that's helpful. so primary goals: reduce unit cost, meet latency SLOs, and keep hybrid relevance. does that sound right?
[02:20] Maya: yep, and ideally keep control of models for audits — so private or dedicated deployment is interesting.
[02:27] James: redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private (vpc/appliance). a lot of teams start on Hosted API to iterate, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput, or Private for strict data residency and KMS-managed keys.
[02:42] Priya: quick q — with Dedicated, do you isolate GPU pools? what's the multi-tenant risk?
[02:48] James: Dedicated is reserved capacity, isolated pools and SLA-backed throughput. in practise you get predictable latency and capacity. Private gives you customer-managed network and KMS/HSM options.
[02:58] Maya: for our flow, the most expensive part is the rerank scoring for top 10 per query. curious how Redwood handles batching and continuous kv-caching to reduce per-token cost.
[03:12] Priya: our runtime does workload-aware batching and prefix/KV cache; we can batch rerank calls across requests when latency window allows and keep kv-cache for repeated contexts. but batching has tradeoffs with p95.
[03:27] Daniel: how does that integrate with Pinecone? we want to continue using our existing vector DB for storage, at least initially.
[03:34] Connor: we see two patterns: 1) keep vector DB (Pinecone) as the storage + nearest-neighbor service and call Redwood for model scoring/rerank; or 2) use Redwood's embeddings pipeline and store vectors in your DB. both are supported.
[03:49] Maya: ok so for option 1, we'd do the ANN search in Pinecone, return top-k ids, then hit Redwood for embedding-based rerank?
[03:56] Priya: yes, you can do external ANN + Redwood for rerank. one useful pattern is to compute embeddings in Redwood and push them to Pinecone via batch export to ensure model consistency.
[04:08] Daniel: any throughput numbers for that flow? our concern is p95 when doing round trip to pinecone + rerank op.
[04:15] Priya: depends on model size and whether you run hosted or dedicated. for small finetuned open models (like your 1024-d vectors generator) Hosted can handle moderate qps but p95 varies; Dedicated with reserved GPUs and batching will give you lower p95 under load. we can run a sizing test with your sample queries to give concrete numbers.
[04:33] Maya: rough cost comparison? storage in pinecone + hosted rerank vs dedicated?
[04:38] James: high level: Hosted is usage-based and good for early pilots; Dedicated moves to committed monthly and lowers per-token compute cost, especially with batching. Storage cost remains with your vector DB. For 100M vectors, we'll show examples of cost curves in the pricing sheet.
[04:55] Ravi: security is huge for us. we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS for keys.
[05:02] James: Redwood has SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs. for Private we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering or on-prem appliance for air-gapped. Priya will share the security brief after the call.
[05:18] Maya: we also need to ensure deterministic embeddings for A/B and evals — model version pinning is important.
[05:24] Priya: we support model pinning and rollout policies; can snapshot model versions used to compute stored vectors. that'll help reproducibility.
[05:33] Daniel: on dimensionality — we're on 1024 dims. any guidance on reducing dims via quantization or projection without losing quality for rerank?
[05:43] Priya: quantization helps storage and memory footprint; we also recommend evaluation runs to test 512 vs 1024 dims. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations and quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[05:58] Maya: do you support hybrid search out-of-the-box? like combining bm25 scores with cosine sims and weighting?
[06:06] Connor: yes, we support hybrid ranking strategies. you can provide the bm25 score as a feature and run a custom reranker model or use a weighted combination. many customers do BM25 -> ANN -> rerank with a small MLP.
[06:22] Daniel: what about latency of using a small MLP reranker?
[06:25] Priya: small rerankers are cheap; the main cost is the forward pass of the model and any embedding calls. again, Dedicated GPUs with batching can amortize.
[06:36] Maya: on integration friction: we have CI/CD pipelines and a bunch of connecting glue — will Redwood APIs fit into our infra?
[06:43] James: yes, we have REST/SDKs, and a consistent config layer. for Private we can provide a control plane that your platform team manages.
[06:53] Ravi: procurement question — what's the minimal commitment for Dedicated?
[06:57] James: typically monthly reserved capacity with a three or six month minimum for entry-level packs, enterprise deals flexible. i'll include exact tiers in the pricing spreadsheet.
[07:07] Maya: what about monitoring? we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards.
[07:13] Priya: Redwood Console has token-level cost/latency, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks and error analysis. you can also export logs to your SIEM.
[07:26] Daniel: can we run a quick hypothetical: 250 qps peak, top-100 bm25, rerank top-10, 1024 dims — what would you recommend?
[07:36] Priya: for 250 qps peak, busiest scenario: Dedicated with autoscaling GPU pools or a hybrid approach where you run Dedicated for peak windows and Hosted for overflow. also evaluate batching latency budgets; if you need sub-300ms p95, we need smaller batch windows or more GPUs.
[07:52] James: another pattern is to precompute embeddings for frequent queries or heavy documents and use prefix caching for popular queries to lower compute.
[07:59] Maya: ok. we're also evaluating Weaviate for schema-based filters — any known integration caveats?
[08:06] Connor: integration is straightforward; filters and metadata need mapping. watch out for inconsistent distance metrics across storages; ensure your ANN index uses dot vs cosine consistently.
[08:19] Daniel: regarding metadata filters, we have heavy boolean filters that reduce candidate sets; does Redwood's reranker handle sparse filtering upstream?
[08:27] Priya: yes, you can pass filtered candidate IDs and metadata, and the reranker will operate on the final candidate list. some customers apply strong prefilters in DB and then do finer rerank in Redwood.
[08:40] Maya: can Redwood host our embedding model or do we self-host?
[08:45] Priya: both: Hosted will run models in our infra; Dedicated/Private can run customer-supplied models. Private allows the most control for model weights and KMS requirements.
[08:56] Ravi: what's the path for model updates and rollouts without regressions?
[09:00] Priya: you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, run evals with your prompt sets, and Redwood Optimize will track regressions.
[09:10] Maya: legal asks about data retention for embeddings — if we use Hosted, do you retain vectors?
[09:16] James: hosted keeps logs for X retention (we'll attach exact policy). Dedicated/Private gives more control; private typically keeps data only in your environment if configured.
[09:28] Sophia: quick clarifying question — does Redwood provide built-in conversion to different vector dims when exporting?
[09:33] Priya: we provide export tooling and support quantized formats, but dimension reduction is something you'd test — we can help run experiments.
[09:42] Daniel: any customers with a similar scale who switched from Pinecone to Redwood-managed vectors?
[09:47] James: yes, a few — we can anonymize case studies, but many keep Pinecone for storage and use Redwood for scoring to reduce migration risk. We'll send references.
[09:59] Maya: i'm worried about cold-start throughput for sudden spikes. how fast can you spin up dedicated capacity?
[10:05] Priya: Dedicated pools have some warm-up time but we support burst capacity and fallback routing. Private on-prem needs planning. We'll propose a fallback policy to use hosted overflow.
[10:18] Ravi: ok interesting. procurement also looks at compliance packages; is there a SOC2 report we can review?
[10:23] James: yes, Priya will share SOC2 and relevant compliance docs after the call.
[10:29] Connor: next i'd like to talk about concrete pilot scope — small pilot where you push embeddings for a subset (10k docs) and we run throughput + p95 measurement under synthetic load.
[10:41] Maya: that sounds good. we'd like to see metrics on p50/p95/p99, cost per query, and quality delta for 512 vs 1024 dims.
[10:50] Priya: we can run that. please share sample dataset and a set of queries. we'll run on Hosted and Dedicated configurations and report back.
[10:59] Daniel: timeline — we want initial results within two weeks if possible.
[11:03] James: we'll aim for a one to two week turnaround once we have data and access.
[11:09] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[11:12] James: recap: 1) Redwood to send pricing and pilot plan; 2) Priya to share security/compliance docs; 3) Avalon to share sample data and QPS expectations; 4) schedule a technical deep dive to run sizing.
[11:28] Ravi: sounds good. thanks all.
[11:31] Maya: thanks everyone.
[11:34] James: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links and attachments.
[11:40] [meeting ended]
